title: Affine-cover criterion for tensor module flatness after base change
statement: Let $A,T$ be commutative rings, $X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ a morphism, and $M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $U_b$, $b\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, be specified affine opens covering $X$. Set $a_b:A\to\Gamma(X,U_b)$ to the map induced by $f$, using the canonical spectrum-sections isomorphism. Let $q:A\to T$, $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and $e:Y\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(T)$ satisfy $\operatorname{Spec}(q)\circ e=p$. Put $D=T\otimes_A A$, with the right $A$-algebra structure, and restrict $\Gamma(M,U_b)$ along $a_b$. The tensor pullback of $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback] to $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}Y$ is flat over $Y$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] if and only if every $D\otimes_A\Gamma(M,U_b)$ is flat over $D$. No finiteness of section rings or modules, limit diagram, or eventual-flatness assertion is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: For each specified affine U_b, the inverse image in X times_{Spec A} Y is affine, using Y = Spec T over Spec A and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Its actual section ring identifies with T tensor_A Gamma(X,U_b), with the base action given by the second projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], quasi-coherent pullback sections identify with T tensor_A Gamma(M,U_b), respecting that action. Locally this pullback is the associated sheaf of the tensor module, so it is quasi-coherent.

The maps T tensor_A A -> T, t tensor r -> t*q(r), and T -> T tensor_A A, t -> t tensor 1, are inverse. Tensor balancing proves the inverse equations and A-linearity for the right A-algebra action. Tensoring gives a scalar-compatible isomorphism (T tensor_A A) tensor_A Gamma(M,U_b) = T tensor_A Gamma(M,U_b). Transport flatness along these ring and module isomorphisms.

If the pullback is relatively flat, evaluate [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] on each pulled-back affine chart and the whole affine base Y. The preceding comparisons give the displayed tensor flatness.

Conversely, tensor flatness makes each chart section module T-flat. Localize at each point; [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base] makes its stalk flat over the corresponding base local ring. The pulled-back charts cover, since U_b cover X. For an arbitrary affine source open over an affine base open, quasi-coherence identifies localizations of its section module with these stalks. Apply [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base], namely Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization and Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal, to obtain every IsFlatOver test directly. The equation he guarantees agreement of the structural maps and scalar actions through e. An empty cover forces X empty, and all stalk tests are vacuous; zero rings and zero modules satisfy the same formulas.
